subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Find the number of ways of arranging the letters of the word MATHEMATICS.

mark_split.label: Count the letters and the repeats

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the arrangements of the word MATHEMATICS — what you count first and which formula you use.
insider_note: MATHEMATICS is 11 letters with three pairs — M, A and T each appear twice — so the divisor is 2!·2!·2! = 8. The T pair is the one most often missed, and each missed pair doubles the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Count the letters and the repeats
steps.margin_note: First mark. M-A-T-H-E-M-A-T-I-C-S: 11 letters. M twice, A twice, T twice; H, E, I, C, S once.
lines: M twice, A twice, T twice.

recall.must_convey: That MATHEMATICS has 11 letters with M, A and T each appearing twice.
accept: eleven letters, M twice, A twice, T twice
count the letters, eleven, with two M, two A and two T
the repeats are M A and T, each two
eleven letters, M A T rendu rendu sarlu vastayi
find the repeated letters first, three pairs

steps.why: Alike letters cannot be told apart, so swapping them does not give a new arrangement. The count of each repeated letter is what the formula divides by, so it must be found before anything else.
common_mistakes: Missing one of the three pairs, usually the T pair.

steps.label: Apply n!/(p!·q!·r!)

recall.must_convey: That the count is 11 factorial over 2 factorial cubed, that is over 8.
accept: eleven factorial over two factorial two factorial two factorial
n factorial by p factorial q factorial r factorial, eleven factorial by two factorial cubed
eleven factorial ni eight tho divide cheyali
the answer is eleven factorial over two factorial two factorial two factorial which is about fifty lakh

steps.why: n! counts the arrangements as if every letter were different; each group of p alike letters has been counted p! times over, so dividing by p! for each group leaves the true count.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 2! once instead of three times.
